short: New attention-before-CTC decoder for lip reading, but one corpus, one run and no attention-only test make it standard; the LRSW row puts a WER in the CER column.
position: LCANet [@xu2018lcanet] changes one component, the decoder (M06): an attention layer placed before a single CTC loss, plus highway layers. The design is new in lip reading (no cascade or hybrid among 57 sentence-level decoder studies before 2018-03), but it is standard: one corpus, one run, no seeds, and an ablation that cannot separate attention from CTC. The gain over LipNet holds on GRID with overlapping speakers, 2.9% against 4.8% WER, and 5.6% without LipNet's language model [@assael2016lipnet]; the comparison with LRSW does not, because Table III puts its 3.0% WER in the CER column [@chung2017was]. The multi-task baseline ranked last is the design of the later best result under the same protocol [@wu2024lcrmi]. M12 is standard: overlapped speakers only, one run.
